verdict: Serve Robotics grew revenue 313% to $2.8M as its delivery robots scaled, but it still spent about $21 for every $1 taken in and lost $59M.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: Net loss per share, vs -$0.54 a year ago

kpis.label: Cash & securities
kpis.note: Cash plus marketable securities at September 30

kpis.label: Daily active robots
kpis.note: Average robots working each day, up from 312 a year ago

segments.name: Fleet services
segments.note: Running the sidewalk delivery robots for delivery platforms and merchants — the delivery work itself. Up 496% YoY as the fleet and daily deliveries grew.

segments.name: Software services
segments.note: Software and related services sold on top of the fleet, including hospital automation work. Roughly flat YoY, and down from $0.9M in Q2 as project timing shifted.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the autonomous robots and their self-driving software. Up 69% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and admin, including a large stock-pay bill. Up 54% YoY on a GAAP basis.

opex.name: Operations
opex.note: The people and overhead who keep the deployed fleet running day to day. Up 143% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Winning delivery partners, merchants and cities. Small, but up from $0.9M a year ago.

otherDetail: Other income was $1.9M, net: $2.0M of interest income on cash and marketable securities, less about $0.1M of small losses and expenses.
follow100Note: Serve is an early-stage company: it spent about $21 for every $1 it took in this quarter, so the $100 view is scaled up accordingly — the loss was covered by cash raised earlier. Delivering the service cost $3.66 for every $1 of revenue, so the gross loss was $7.6M before any running costs.

takeaways.title: Growth is real — and so is the scale gap
takeaways.text: Revenue rose to $2.8M from $0.7M a year ago. The average fleet grew to 917 robots working daily (from 312), daily delivery volume among new partners tripled, and recurring revenue was 69% of the total. Management raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $12M.

takeaways.title: Each delivery still costs more than it earns
takeaways.text: Cost of revenue was $10.4M against $2.8M of revenue — a gross loss of $7.6M, though the margin improved a lot from a year ago (when delivery cost $7.37 per $1 of revenue) and from Q2. The company says fleet margins improved more than 100 percentage points sequentially as volume spread the fixed costs.

takeaways.title: The bottom line is funded by the balance sheet
takeaways.text: Total operating costs were $53.6M — research, admin, operations and sales — producing a $59.2M net loss. A large share is stock pay: on the company's non-GAAP basis (leaving out stock compensation and similar items) the loss was $44.6M. Serve held $198M in cash and securities at quarter end.

oneTimers: GAAP costs include substantial non-cash stock-based compensation: the company's non-GAAP figures put Q3 operating costs at $39.2M vs $53.6M GAAP, and the non-GAAP net loss at $44.6M vs $59.2M GAAP.
footerNote: Serve reports in thousands; figures here are exact to the thousand, shown in $M. How this chart is drawn: delivering the service cost $10.4M against $2.8M of revenue, so gross profit was negative (-$7.6M) and there is no 'after direct costs' profit step to show. Instead, the slate 'Covered by cash on hand' block — the quarter's $59.2M net loss, funded from the $198M Serve held in cash and securities — is drawn paying the $7.6M delivery-cost gap and then the running costs, with $1.9M of interest income and a $0.1M tax benefit also flowing into running costs.
